products.name: Code.org
products.note: Verified in the research for The AI Ready School. AI: AI Lab features not verified. Use: Computer science courses and AI lessons. Who: Students K to 12, teachers. Student age: Designed for all ages; under 13 with school, teacher, or parent pre-authorization; teacher-created alias accounts; sharing limited under 13. Privacy: Student Privacy Pledge signatory; districts can sign Code.org's student data privacy addendum online, with state versions for New York, Illinois, and Montana. Price: Free.

profile_text.body:
Code.org (nonprofit) is described on its site as an education innovation nonprofit with the vision that every student in every school has the opportunity to learn about artificial intelligence and computer science as part of core K-12 education. The site states that 84% of students already use AI, while only 16% of high school leaders say all their students are learning about it in school. It offers free curriculum and teacher professional development, and says no prior experience is needed to teach it. The site describes a free, flexible high school curriculum where students go from understanding how AI works to building web apps with AI as a creative partner, a free middle school course centered on digital fluency, and an introduction to AI and machine learning for young students that emphasizes pattern-based logic. The site also announces a partnership with OpenAI and says AI Discoveries and AI Foundations: Designing and Building with AI are now in classrooms. The site lists Hour of AI and CS Discoveries as trademarks, notes that "Code.org" is a former trademark, and carries a 2026 copyright notice.

The company's tracked product is Code.org, listed under Education and Research AI. It covers computer science courses and AI lessons for students in kindergarten through 12th grade and for teachers, is designed for all ages, and is free. Students under 13 require school, teacher, or parent pre-authorization, use teacher-created alias accounts, and have limited sharing. Code.org is a Student Privacy Pledge signatory, and districts can sign its student data privacy addendum online, with state versions for New York, Illinois, and Montana. The site's AI Lab features are noted as not verified.
